- **D-0074** scope=N-0086: Client-IP trust for the login throttle (N-0086): the web listens on 127.0.0.1 only (supervisor-enforced), so its peers are cloudflared or local processes. The Next proxy drops every visitor-supplied client-address header (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, Forwarded, CF-Connecting-IP(v6), True-Client-IP, X-Client-IP, X-Cluster-Client-IP) and sends exactly one address upstream in X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP: CF-Connecting-IP when it is a single valid IP literal (set and overwritten by the Cloudflare edge for tunnel traffic), otherwise 127.0.0.1. The API (127.0.0.1:8001) honours X-Forwarded-For only from a loopback peer (right-most entry; uvicorn's default proxy-header trust of 127.0.0.1 gives the same answer) and keys the throttle on IPv4, IPv4-mapped IPv6 as IPv4, other IPv6 per /64. Rejected: trusting X-Forwarded-For from the tunnel (visitor-controlled); using the TCP peer (always loopback, would make one global bucket for all tunnel users). Residual: a local process can forge CF-Connecting-IP but can already reach the API directly; all non-tunnel local traffic shares one 127.0.0.1 bucket; if the web is ever bound wider than loopback, LAN clients also share that bucket (fails closed, not open). Reversible by code revert; no data change.
